principles: Preserve assertion INTENT, only realign TEXT/REGEX/ENUM to current production output
Production regressions get filed + split (do NOT silently work around)
drivers: B-c6cf CHK-002:happy:2 waiver needs retiring for CI viability
Test signal is unreliable — every failure looks like noise
One batch beats 24 stories (Lattice overhead would dominate)

options.name: (a) one big batch story (chosen)
pros: Pattern repeats — one diff is easier to audit collectively
cons: Large diff surface in test code

options.name: (b) cluster: assertion vs timeout vs race

rationale: User picked (a) on 2026-06-17. Pattern is uniform (stale assertions); batch is efficient. Production-regression escape hatch documented in scope-boundary so we do not silently mask real bugs.

preMortem.scenario: A failing smoke is actually catching a real production regression
preMortem.trigger: DEV finds the assertion was right; production behavior is the wrong one
preMortem.consequence: Fixing the assertion would silently hide a real bug
preMortem.mitigation: Implementer MUST file finding_add severity=high describing the regression, leave the smoke broken, split the prod fix to a follow-up story. scope-boundary documents this escape hatch.

preMortem.scenario: Fixing assertions in one smoke breaks another (shared fixture/global state)
preMortem.trigger: After fixing N smokes, smoke N+1 starts failing for new reasons
preMortem.mitigation: Run npm run test:all at the END of every commit during DEV, not just at the end of the story. Catch shared-state coupling early.

preMortem.scenario: lattice-baseline TIMEOUT is a real deadlock
preMortem.trigger: Raising timeoutMs makes test:all run for hours but still TIMEOUT
preMortem.mitigation: If after 2 attempts the TIMEOUT persists, file finding severity=high, set skip:true on the manifest entry with a comment pointing to the finding, defer real fix to follow-up.

preMortem.scenario: Parallel-only race failures are not deterministically reproducible
preMortem.trigger: A smoke fails in test:all (parallel) but passes in test:coverage (--jobs 1)
preMortem.mitigation: Run npm run test:all 3 times consecutively after a fix; require all 3 to pass. If still flaky, treat as production-rooted and file finding.
